title: Nitrogen-use efficiency in cereals
bottleneck: Cereals recover only 30–50% of applied nitrogen fertilizer; the rest leaches into waterways or volatilizes as nitrous oxide, a potent greenhouse gas. Every tonne of wheat carries about 20 kg of nitrogen off the field, and the Haber-Bosch process that replaces it consumes roughly 2% of global energy. Breeding for nitrogen-use efficiency has made slow progress because the trait is complex and trades off against yield under high-input conditions.
why_it_blocks: Nitrogen is simultaneously the ceiling on yields and one of agriculture's largest environmental costs. Without efficient crops, feeding the world means poisoning its water and climate.
current_state: NUE breeding and precision application improve efficiency incrementally; no step-change variety exists. Precision application and slow-release fertilizers improve efficiency incrementally; no step-change variety exists.
